---
title: "Setup guide"
---

This sets up everything you need for the semester: Git, Positron (the editor),
uv (which builds the course's Python environment), and your private course repo
on GitHub. Do it before the second class session. If you get stuck, see the
[Setup FAQ](setup-faq.qmd).

**Before you start:** about 5 GB of free disk space, an internet connection, and
your WSU login. On a Chromebook or iPad, skip to [No-install path](#no-install).

## Steps

1. **GitHub account.** Sign up at [github.com](https://github.com) with any
   username (it doesn't need to be your real name) and add your WSU email to the
   account. Then apply for GitHub Education student benefits at
   [education.github.com](https://education.github.com); approval can take a few
   days. Enter your username in the Canvas "GitHub username" survey.
2. **Git.**
   - *Windows:* install "Git for Windows" from [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com)
     and accept every default. It includes the sign-in helper Git needs for GitHub.
   - *Mac:* open Terminal, type `git --version`, and accept the prompt to install
     the Command Line Tools. Then install the GitHub CLI from
     [cli.github.com](https://cli.github.com) and run `gh auth login` (choose the
     web-browser login) and `gh auth setup-git`, so Git can sign in to GitHub.
3. **Positron.** Download and install it from
   [positron.posit.co](https://positron.posit.co).
4. **uv.**
   - *Windows* (PowerShell):
     `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"`
   - *Mac* (Terminal): `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`

   Close and reopen the terminal afterward.
5. **Tell Git who you are** (in a terminal):

   ```
   git config --global user.name "First Last"
   git config --global user.email "your-github-email@example.com"
   ```
6. **Accept your repo invitation** from the email GitHub sends you, or at
   `https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>/invitations`.
7. **Clone your repo.** Make a folder such as `EconS431` directly in your home
   folder (`C:\Users\<you>\EconS431` or `/Users/<you>/EconS431`). **Not in
   OneDrive, Dropbox, or iCloud, and not on your Desktop or in Documents**, which
   many laptops sync automatically. Then, in a Positron terminal:

   ```
   cd ~/EconS431
   git clone https://github.com/WSU-EconS431/ps-<your-username>.git
   ```

   The first clone opens a GitHub sign-in window; choose the browser option.
   Then open the new folder: **File > Open Folder** > `EconS431/ps-<your-username>`.
8. **Build the environment.** In a Positron terminal inside your repo, run
   `uv sync`. Then click the interpreter name at the top right and choose the
   Python from `.venv` (labeled **econs431**). If Positron offers to create an
   environment, decline: `uv sync` builds the course one.
9. **Check it.** Run `uv run python check_setup.py`. Every line should start with
   `[OK]`. Then open `ps00/ps00.ipynb`, choose the same **econs431** kernel at the
   top right of the notebook, complete it, commit, push, and submit the commit
   link in Canvas.

## No-install path {#no-install}

For a Chromebook, an iPad, or a laptop that won't cooperate: do steps 1 and 6.
Then, on your repo's GitHub page, click **Code > Codespaces > Create codespace**.
Wait for setup to finish (a few minutes the first time) and start at step 9.

## Every problem set

1. **Pull** in Positron (Source Control > **...** > Pull). The new `psNN/` folder appears.
2. **Work** in `psNN/psNN.ipynb`, and commit whenever something works.
3. **Restart & Run All.** If it doesn't run from top to bottom, it isn't finished.
4. **Fill in the AI usage note** at the bottom.
5. **Push, copy the commit URL** from GitHub, and **paste it into Canvas** before
   the deadline.

## Rules of the road

- Your repo is private. Never make it public or share it, even after the course,
  unless an assignment says it may be shared.
- Use relative paths (`data/prices.csv`), never `C:\Users\...`. Your code must
  run on the instructor's machine.
- Don't commit `.venv/` or big data files. GitHub rejects files over 100 MB, and
  your repo's `.gitignore` handles the common cases.
- Don't change `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`. If you think you need another
  package, ask on Discussions.
- **Asking for help:** see [Getting help](setup-faq.qmd#getting-help).
